Command

command is the shared, UI-free registry for application engines. It owns Command<S>, Registry<S>, Described, Error, Scope, Origin, Executed, Journal and Fluent Strings. Its public contract is 0.3.0. There are no egui or windowing dependencies.

Registry::execute(id, state, params, origin) looks up the command, calls the optional authorize hook, checks enablement, refuses parameters on nullary commands, then runs the handler and returns its JSON result. Refusals are Unknown, Denied { id, reason }, Disabled { id, reason }, BadParams { id, msg } or Failed. Only successful handlers are journaled. Queries skip the journal; intent, input and system commands are recorded.

Handlers with parameters declare ParamSpec { type_name, schema }, derive schemars::JsonSchema on their serde request struct, and deserialize with deny_unknown_fields, mapping decoding errors to BadParams. Schema reporting does not itself validate a request. Nullary commands accept JSON null or an empty object; other input is refused. The nullary!(id, label, handler) macro wraps an existing fn(&mut S) as an intent returning JSON null.

describe(state, strings) keeps id, label, menu, shortcut, more, enabled and checked. It adds reason (null when enabled), class (intent, query, input, system) and schema (null for nullary commands). Empty more is still omitted. The authorisation hook sees id, origin and params at dispatch; describe reports state enablement, since it has no caller or parameter body.

Shortcuts and Lucide icon names are strings. Bindings, conflict policy, overrides, choices, toggles, scopes and changing labels live here. An adapter supplies chord validation when applying a keymap. Strings handles Fluent catalogues; Labels allows an adapter to supply catalogue fallbacks.

Toolkit retains egui shortcut parsing, event handling, menus and palette rendering. Its existing nullary Command, CommandError and three-argument Registry::execute remain compatibility wrappers, so existing application tables need no edits. It re-exports the moved data types. New engine-owned tables use toolkit::action::EngineAdapter::new(registry): it caches parsed shortcuts and resolved icons and dispatches typed parameters through the original registry.

Executed events are v2: v, run, seq, at_ms, id, origin, params, result, then dropped. The accepted params are preserved verbatim, including null; nullary runs store null params and note() stores null for both fields. The result is the handler's returned value. Each field above 4096 compact JSON bytes is replaced with { bytes, sha256 }, the byte count and lowercase SHA-256 of serde_json::to_vec output. executed::bounded and executed::EXECUTED_RESULT_BYTES expose that policy. note and take_executed remain available through toolkit for citizen's publisher, which updates dropped.

ExecuteRequest { id, params } is the body type referenced by every <app>.execute row in command registry schema 4. It derives serde and JsonSchema, refuses unknown fields, and defaults omitted or null params to None. Existing apps retain their current parsers during migration.

Authorisation refusal returns Denied before checking enablement, parameters or running the handler. Toolkit maps it to legacy CommandError::Denied. Both adapters report stored shortcut and more strings in the keymaps grammar, in Ctrl, Alt, Shift order. Keys preserve the stored spelling, such as ArrowLeft or Left, =, - and /.

The application layering table (apps/layers.conf.mix) prevents engine dependency paths from reaching GUI crates, including through another workspace library. Unit and integration tests cover dispatch, schema reporting, journals and the toolkit shortcut behaviour.

History

command::History<D> holds bounded Arc<D> snapshots for a cloneable, comparable document state. History::new(initial, history::Budget { max_entries, max_bytes, bytes }) bounds retained undo and redo snapshots; the current state and saved checkpoint are retained separately. The byte function measures one snapshot, conservatively counting shared allocations. Edits clone the current state and commit only on success. Failed edits leave the state, checkpoint and both stacks untouched. New edits clear redo.

edit(label, closure) starts an undo step; consecutive edit_coalesced(key, closure) calls with the same key share a step. An ordinary edit, undo, redo or mark_saved() ends the coalescing group. current(), can_undo(), can_redo(), depth() and labels() expose state without mutation. mark_saved() records a checkpoint; dirty() compares document values.
